## Core Principles

### I. Platform Owns Infrastructure (NON-NEGOTIABLE)
This service runs on Stacktic. Infrastructure is DECLARED as components and links on the
stack diagram and GENERATED by the platform — it is never written by hand and never by an
AI agent. Any plan step that creates Kubernetes manifests, Terraform, Dockerfiles for
infra, connection plumbing, or credentials handling is a constitution violation. The
correct action is a stack design change via the Stacktic MCP: `design(action=add|connect|
modify|remove)` — or asking the operator to draw the link.

### II. The Environment Contract Is Law
The application consumes ONLY the environment variables generated by the platform for this
component. Their exact names live in the stack repo (source of truth, regenerated on every
stack change): `external_source_code/catalog-svc/k8s/config/cloud.env`
and the secret env in `k8s/secret/`. Never hardcode an endpoint, credential, port, or
connection string. Need an env the links do not provide? It goes into the component's
`configmap` attribute (KEY=VALUE) via the platform — not into code or manifests.

### III. Wiring Facts (generated — this service's links)
Framework: `django` | Container port: `8000` (Service exposes 80; `SERVICE_PORT` is set)
- outbound link `external_source_code-db` → `catalog-db`
- outbound link `external_source_code-swbucket` → `catalog-images`

Every one of these links auto-generates env, credentials, network policies. Treat this

### IV. Test Against the Live Contract
Acceptance criteria must be verifiable against the RUNNING stack (Stacktic stack-tests /
`stack_test` via the MCP), not only unit tests. "Done" means the deployed service passes
its spec-derived checks.

### V. Source of Truth Over Assumption
`stack-metadata.yaml` at the stack-repo root declares every component, attribute, link and
sub-component. When a plan needs a platform fact, read it there or ask the Stacktic MCP
(`knowledge`, `graph`, `stacktic_get`) — never assume.
